title: Sidekiq jobs, retries, and cache freshness
outcome: Make a job safe to repeat and explain when cached data may be old.
cue: Later means changed. Retry means repeat.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: Two workers both see sent? false and send a receipt. Repair the local race and explain the remote uncertainty.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A user revokes access but a cached task remains visible for an hour. How do you change the read path?

trace.title: Saved intent
trace.detail:
# The idea

A background job runs later and may run more than once. Pass small JSON-friendly arguments, usually IDs, rather than whole model objects.

The row may have changed or disappeared before the worker starts.

Sidekiq 5 uses include Sidekiq::Worker for a direct worker. Modern Sidekiq examples can use newer APIs; keep that version difference visible.

A successful enqueue is not proof that work completed. Monitor queue latency, retries, and terminal failures.

Idempotent means repeating the same logical command does not create another logical effect. A seen? pre-check can race.

Use a database uniqueness rule for local effects and a stable provider idempotency key when the remote API supports it. A cache stores a copy; define its key, expiry, and invalidation.

Tenant/user context may belong in the key.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Trace enqueue → delayed start → load current row → attempt external effect → timeout → retry. The timeout does not say whether the provider accepted the action.

Reusing the same logical key lets a supporting provider deduplicate it.

For a cache, trace miss → compute → store → hit → underlying update → expiry/invalidation. Record what maximum staleness the user can accept.

A permission decision should not use an indefinitely stale shared cache.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail:
Testing Sidekiq inline changes timing and can hide a transaction visibility bug. Enqueueing before commit can let a worker read data that is not committed yet.

A cache key without tenant scope can leak another tenant’s result.
